- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to catch upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 2–5%.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (especially after sentiment turns positive); add 1–3% buffer for final 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment trend direction.
